newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba regrets loss of life in Peru hostage siege.
newsitem.headline: Cuba regrets loss of life in Peru hostage siege.

text.p: Cuba, which had offered political asylum to the guerrillas in the Peruvian hostage siege, said on Thursday it regretted that 17 people died when Peruvian commandos ended the 126-day ordeal in a raid.

"We regret that human lives have been lost," acting Foreign Ministry spokesman Alejandro Gonzalez said. But he carefully avoided passing any judgment on the method chosen by the Peruvian government to end the crisis.
"This is an internal matter of the Peruvians," he told a news briefing.

Cuba had offered to help bring about a peaceful solution to the crisis by allowing the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas asylum in the Communist-ruled island if they released their hostages.
All 14 of the guerrillas, one hostage and two Peruvian commandos were killed in the military assault on the Japanese amabassador's residence in Lima where the hostages were held.

From the outset, Cuba sought to keep a low profile in the hostage drama by avoiding public judgments. President Fidel Castro had stressed that the offer of possible asylum for the MRTA guerrillas was made purely on humanitarian grounds.

Foreign diplomats said the Cuban government, which has a history of links with armed Latin American leftist groups, appeared anxious that its participation in a possible solution should not be interpreted as support for violent actions like the MRTA seizure of the ambassador's residence.
